title: Azerbaijani TTS (9.36M, 24 kHz, offline)
subtitle: Offline Azerbaijani text-to-speech, 2-4x real time on CPU
description:
A fully offline text-to-speech model that speaks Azerbaijani. 9.36M parameters, 24 kHz mono, 2-4x faster than real time on an ordinary laptop CPU, and it needs no internet at runtime - which makes it usable inside a Kaggle notebook with networking switched off.

Adapted from owensong/Inflect-Micro-v2 (Apache-2.0) with 200,000 training steps over 25.07 hours of Azerbaijani audio. The warm start was complete: 409 of 410 tensors were copied bit-identically from the base model.

Code, tests and the full training pipeline: https://github.com/INSERT_GITHUB_USER/azerbaycan-tts

Limitations: one voice, no emotion control, no voice cloning. At 9.36M parameters the speech is clear but not fully natural, and the vocoder can leave a metallic resonance. The training audio is most likely synthetic, so the quality ceiling is the system that produced it.

Training data: ughurabbasov/azerbaijani-tts-dataset. The dataset declares no licence file; its author confirmed in the HuggingFace community tab that anyone may use it, with attribution requested.

Runtime note: phonemisation goes through phonemizer and eSpeak NG, both GPL-3.0-or-later. Running is unaffected; redistributing a combined work brings those terms with it. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md in the repository.

Do not use this voice to impersonate a real person or to produce deceptive content.
